quantifier: There exist alpha_1 > 0 and a finite uniform U such that, for every alpha in (0, alpha_1), d_W <= U sqrt(alpha) log(1/alpha).
assumptions: d-dimensional globally Lipschitz C2 drift with bounded second derivatives
Hurwitz Jacobian and unique stationary law
uniform third stationary moment for iid noise or fourth moment for Markov noise
iid centered positive-definite covariance and finite third noise moment, or Assumption 4.1 finite-state Markov conditions
operationalization: d=8 separable assumption-satisfying SGD, linear, and contractive systems; coordinate W1 distances rigorously bracket the Euclidean product-law W1.
acceptance: All iid and Markov model families satisfy a held-out sqrt(alpha) log(1/alpha) upper envelope.
The closed-form Gaussian linear-SA checker independently satisfies the same upper rate.
At least four wrong O(alpha) negative-control envelopes fail on held-out stepsizes.
